Hi, I'm Yesid Barrios.

24 years old — Software Engineering Student & Athlete

I am a 24-year-old Software Engineering student living in Barrio El Milagro, Magangué. I am passionate about technology, programming, and outdoor sports. In my free time, I love riding my mountain bike across the city, training at the gym in downtown with my friend, jogging early in the morning at the patinódromo, watching movies at the cinema, and doing long weekend rides to Puente Roncador. On weekends, I always cheer for Real Madrid!

Where I Love to Go 5 Places

Here are 5 of my favorite spots in Magangué, featuring authentic photos, exact street addresses, travel times from my home in El Milagro, and imperative directions.

01 · Best Gym in Town (Downtown)
By Bicycle (30 min)
📍 Address: Calle 16 / Av. Colombia, Sector Comercial, Centro de Magangué

1. The Downtown Gym (Best in the City)

👥 With: My workout partner (friend) 📅 Frequency: Regular weekday training

Even though it is the farthest gym from my house (a 30-minute bike ride to downtown), I always go there to accompany my friend. It is recognized as the best and most complete gym in Magangué, located in the commercial downtown sector.

Imperative Directions (Unit 3) How to get there from El Milagro: Take your bicycle from my house in Barrio El Milagro, ride straight along Avenida Colombia towards downtown for 30 minutes, turn right at the commercial square on Calle 16, and enter the gym on the second floor.
02 · Outdoor Cardio & Jogging
By Bicycle (15 min)
📍 Address: Carrera 20 #20-75 (Complejo Hernando Padauí), Magangué

2. El Patinódromo (Skating & Jogging Track)

👥 With: Friends & training partners 📅 Frequency: Early morning workouts

This is our sports track (Complejo Deportivo Hernando Padauí) located on Carrera 20. It takes me only 15 minutes by bicycle from my house in El Milagro. I love jogging around the circuit early at dawn while enjoying the fresh morning breeze.

Imperative Directions (Unit 3) How to get there from El Milagro: Pedal your bicycle north from my neighborhood, continue straight along the central avenue for 15 minutes to Carrera 20, cross the pedestrian boulevard safely, and enter the sports complex gates on your right.
03 · Entertainment (Éxito Shopping Center)
By Mototaxi / Bike (20 min)
📍 Address: Calle 16 #10-201 (Almacén Éxito Magangué), Bolívar

3. The Cinema (At Éxito Shopping Center)

👥 With: My close friends 📅 Frequency: Once or twice a month

The cinema is located inside the Éxito department store complex at Calle 16 #10-201, about 20 minutes from my home. I love going there with friends on weekend evenings to watch new movie premieres and enjoy popcorn.

Imperative Directions (Unit 3) How to get there from El Milagro: Take a mototaxi or ride your bike towards Calle 16 #10-201, ride for about 20 minutes, enter through the main entrance of Éxito, and walk straight to the cinema ticket office.
04 · Mountain Bike Route (24.2 km / 48.4 km RT)
By Mountain Bike (~1h 15 min · 24.2 km)
📍 Address: Carretera 78 & Vía Juan Arias - Yatí, Magangué

4. Puente Roncador (Magdalena River Bridge)

👥 With: My cycling friends 📅 Frequency: Weekend adventure rides 📏 Distance: 24.2 km one-way (48.4 km round-trip)

I recently bought a high-performance mountain bike, and this is our ultimate long-distance cycling challenge. The route from Magangué to Puente Roncador is exactly 24.2 kilometers one-way (about 48.4 km round-trip) along Carretera 78 via the Juan Arias - Magangué corridor and Yatí. It takes around 1 hour and 15 minutes of energetic pedaling. Puente Roncador spans 2.3 km across the Magdalena River, rewarding us with fresh river breezes and spectacular panoramic views.

Imperative Directions (Unit 3) How to get there from El Milagro: Leave my house in Barrio El Milagro, pedal north along the Juan Arias-Magangué corridor, continue straight on Carretera 78 past Yatí for 24.2 km, ride across the 2.3-kilometer bridge over the Magdalena River, and stop at the scenic lookout to hydrate, rest, and enjoy the sunrise.
05 · Parque El Camajón (Barrio La Florida)
By Bike / Walk (20 min)
📍 Address: Barrio La Florida / El Camajón (Sector Polideportivo), Magangué

5. Parque El Camajón (In Barrio La Florida)

👥 With: My friend who lives in La Florida 📅 Frequency: Frequently in the afternoons & evenings

This community sports park is called El Camajón, situated in Barrio La Florida, about 20 minutes from my home. I visit this park because a good friend lives right around there. It features a community soccer pitch (cancha de fútbol) and shaded benches where we sit, talk, relax, and listen to music.

Imperative Directions (Unit 3) How to get there from El Milagro: Leave my house in El Milagro, head north-west towards Barrio La Florida for about 20 minutes, locate Parque El Camajón, enter the park grounds, and meet my friend on the benches next to the soccer pitch.

Places I Rarely Visit 5 Places

These are 5 locations in and around Magangué that I don't visit often, along with authentic photos, real locations, and the exact personal reasons why.

1. The Cathedral (Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria)

Why I don't visit: I am a Christian, so I do not attend Catholic church services. Additionally, the cathedral is located downtown by the riverbank, which is quite far from my neighborhood.

Address: Plaza de la Candelaria, Calle 11 con Carrera 2 (Centro Histórico)

2. Nightclubs & Bars (Discotecas)

Why I don't visit: I lead a clean, athletic lifestyle and I do not drink any alcohol at all. Noisy clubs are simply not my scene; I prefer sports and music in peaceful environments.

Address: Avenida Colombia & Commercial Corridors across town

3. The Local Stadium (Diego de Carvajal)

Why I don't visit: Located in Barrio Santa Rita (just past my neighborhood), there are almost never any good or exciting sports events happening here. I prefer watching major international soccer matches of Real Madrid at home.

Address: Barrio Santa Rita (Calle 12 / Cra. 40), South Sector

4. Nearby Surrounding Towns (Pueblos Aledaños)

Why I don't visit: The nearby rural towns (like Cascajal or Coyongal) are far away from the urban area, and the rural roads can be quite dangerous and isolated to travel, especially alone.

Address: Rural Corregimientos (Cascajal, Coyongal, Barranco de Yuca)

5. The Fluvial Port & Passenger Terminal (Puerto Fluvial)

Why I don't visit often: Located at the passenger boat terminal on the Magdalena riverbank, it is quite far from my house. I only ever go there on rare occasions when a relative arrives by riverboat and I go to pick them up.

Address: Terminal Fluvial de Pasajeros / Muelle La Albarrada (Norte)
